name: Groq API token pricing (serverless LPU, per 1M tokens, 2026-10-04 list price)
region: Groq cloud (US); no regional GPU SKU to price
price_basis: USD per 1M TOKENS, LIST PRICE, observed 2026-10-04. openai/gpt-oss-20b $0.075 input / $0.30 output at 1000 tok/s; openai/gpt-oss-120b $0.15 / $0.60 at 500 tok/s; qwen/qwen3.8-27b $0.80 / $4.00 at 450 tok/s; openai/safety-gpt-oss-20b $0.075 / $0.30. Speech is priced by time not tokens: whisper-large-v3 $0.111 per hour, whisper-large-v3-turbo $0.04 per hour. Content-moderation models are priced per 1M tokens AND per 1M CHARACTERS on the same page (Canopy Labs Orpheus V1 English $22.00 per 1M characters, Arabic Saudi $40.00). price_usd = gpt-oss-20b input.
notes:
Two things make Groq's page structurally different from the others. First, its headline Llama models are NOT on the public list price at all: llama-3.1-8b-instant and llama-3.3-70b-versatile both read literally 'ContactSales' in the price column. So the cheapest commonly-quoted Groq number in circulation is stale - Llama 3.3 70B on Groq moved to sales-gated pricing, and only the gpt-oss / Qwen / guard models remain self-serve. Second, Groq publishes SPEED next to price on the same row (1000 and 500 tok/s for the gpt-oss models), which makes it the only provider here where throughput is a published list attribute rather than something you benchmark yourself. For character-priced models, tokens are the wrong unit - $22 per 1M CHARACTERS on a TTS-style model is not comparable to a $2 per 1M token input rate at all. No GPU hourly rate is published.

 EXPORT CONTROL (2026-10-04): NOT APPLICABLE IN THE HARDWARE-SHIPMENT SENSE - this record prices a token-based API, so no accelerator is transferred across a border and the ECCN 3A090 hardware licence regime does not attach to the transaction. Recorded null rather than false precisely because a token API is where export control instead becomes an END-USER/TERMS question: the provider applies geographic and end-user restrictions to service access (the AI Diffusion Rule briefly put a tiered country structure on exactly this kind of service before being rescinded on 2025-05-13), and a customer can still be refused under sanctions or end-use policy regardless of where the compute sits. Anyone reading this record for a restricted destination should look at the provider's terms, not at the EAR. Sources for the regime: spl-bis-2025-05-ai-diffusion-rescission, spl-bis-2026-05-d5-guidance.

For a restricted destination, read the provider's terms, not the EAR. Sources: spl-bis-2025-05-ai-diffusion-rescission, spl-bis-2026-05-d5-guidance.

 LEAD TIME: null - correct and not a gap. A token-priced serverless API is provisioned on request, so there is no lead time to publish; the binding constraint when a model is at capacity is provider-side queuing and any per-account concurrency limit, which this repo records in notes where a vendor publishes one (see the DeepSeek concurrency figures already here). Deliberately NOT recorded: any 'model capacity lead time' estimate, because vendors publish none and the SEO 'GPU lead time' numbers that circulate do not apply to a rented endpoint. Probe log in source spl-negative-no-oem-publishes-lead-time.

 ACCELERATOR LINK ADDED 2026-10-04: Groq serves on its own LPU ([[accelerators/groq-lpu]]), not on a rented GPU, which is why Groq is the one provider here where published throughput (1000 tok/s gpt-oss-20b, 500 tok/s gpt-oss-120b) is a list attribute rather than something you benchmark - there is no commodity GPU behind the rate to be throttled by.
